source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice short questions written from Chapter 13 (PDF 291-304), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 13 (Halogens) ke poore chapter se practice short questions (mukhtasar sawal) hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein, Board ke 2 number wale sawal ke andaz mein. Har sawal ka mukhtasar model jawab hai; chhote numericals mein hal ke qadam hain, aur farq wale sawal ka jawab table mein hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 What are halogens? Name the common members of the family.
(Halogens kya hain? Is family ke aam members ke naam likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Halogens periodic table ke Group 17 (VIIA) ke elements hain: bohat reactive non-metals jin ki chemical properties milti julti hain. Aam members fluorine, chlorine, bromine aur iodine hain; astatine aur tennessine bohat kam milte aur radioactive (tabkari) hain.

book_ref.quote: Elements present in Group 17 or VIIA of the periodic table are termed as halogens

blocks.prompt:
2 How did the halogens get their name?
(Halogens ka naam kaise para?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh naam Greek alfaaz 'halos' (namak) aur 'gen' (banana) se bana hai; yani halogen ka matlab hai namak banane wala.

book_ref.quote: meaning “salt”, and “gen”, meaning “to make.”

blocks.prompt:
3 State the physical state and colour of each common halogen at room temperature.
(Room temperature par har aam halogen ki halat aur rang batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Sab diatomic molecules hain. F₂: halki zard gas; Cl₂: sabz-zard gas; Br₂: surkhi-mayl bhoora volatile liquid jis ke fumes corrosive aur zehreele hain; I₂: chamakdar greyish black solid jo sublime ho kar violet vapour banta hai.

book_ref.quote: Halogens exist as diatomic molecules in all phases (gas, liquid or solid)

blocks.prompt:
4 Why do the colours of the halogens darken from chlorine to iodine?
(Chlorine se iodine tak halogens ke rang gehre kyun hote hain?)
blocks.explanation: Rang darja ba darja gehra hota hai kyunke har halogen ke molecules ke andar electron transitions ki wajah se light ka absorption (jazb) badalta hai.

book_ref.quote: due to changes in the absorption of light as a result of electron transitions

blocks.prompt:
5 Chlorine is poisonous. Is it of any use to the human body?
(Chlorine zehreeli hai. Kya yeh insaani jism ke liye kisi kaam ki hai?)
blocks.explanation: Haan. Chlorine zehreeli hai, lekin chloride ki shakal mein is ki thodi miqdaar insaani sehat aur zindagi ke liye zaroori hai.

book_ref.quote: small amount is essential to human health and life in the form of chloride

blocks.prompt:
6 Write the electron shell structure and outer shell configuration of chlorine and iodine (Table 13.1).
(Chlorine aur iodine ki electron shell structure aur outer shell configuration likhein (Table 13.1).)
blocks.explanation: Chlorine (Z = 17): 2, 8, 7; outer shell 3s²3p⁵. Iodine (Z = 53): 2, 8, 18, 18, 7; outer shell 5s²5p⁵. Dono ke outer shell mein saat electrons hain.

book_ref.quote: Outer shell electron configuration

blocks.text: 13.1 Volatility of chlorine, bromine and iodine

blocks.prompt:
7 Arrange chlorine, bromine and iodine in order of decreasing volatility and give the state of each at room temperature.
(Chlorine, bromine aur iodine ko ghat-ti volatility ki tarteeb mein likhein aur room temperature par har aik ki halat batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂. Chlorine gas hai (hawa mein jaldi phailti hai), bromine liquid hai jo aasani se urr kar zehreele fumes deta hai, aur iodine solid hai, sab se kam volatile.

book_ref.quote: At room temperature chlorine is a gas (bromine is the liquid and iodine a solid)

blocks.prompt:
8 Give three reasons why volatility decreases from chlorine to iodine.
(Chlorine se iodine tak volatility kam hone ki teen wajoohat likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Group mein neeche: (i) molecular mass barhta hai; (ii) outer shell ka size barhta hai; (iii) intermolecular forces (London dispersion forces) mazboot hoti hain. Mazboot forces molecules ko jore rakhti hain, is liye volatility kam hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: This trend is due to the increasing molecular mass, increase in size of outer shell and stronger intermolecular forces

blocks.prompt:
9 Why is bromine named from the Greek word 'bromos'?
(Bromine ka naam Greek lafz 'bromos' se kyun rakha gaya?)
blocks.explanation: 'Bromos' ka matlab badboo hai. Bromine liquid room temperature par aasani se urr kar orange vapour deta hai jis ki boo bohat tez aur buri hai.

book_ref.quote: Bromine has a very strong and bad odor.

blocks.text: 13.2 Trend in volatility of the halogens

blocks.prompt:
10 Which intermolecular forces act between halogen molecules, and why only these?
(Halogen molecules ke darmiyan kaun si intermolecular forces hoti hain, aur sirf yahi kyun?)
blocks.explanation: Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole (id-id ya London dispersion) forces. Halogen molecules X₂ non-polar hain (do aik jaise atoms), is liye in mein mustaqil dipole nahi; sirf waqti dipoles inhein khenchte hain.

book_ref.quote: Halogens are non-polar and instantaneous dipole-induced forces play a significant role

blocks.prompt:
11 How are volatility and boiling point related? Explain with a reason.
(Volatility aur boiling point ka kya taaluq hai? Wajah ke saath samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation: Volatility boiling point ke ulat hai: zyada volatile substance ka boiling point kam hota hai. Mazboot intermolecular forces mein molecules ko liquid se gas mein alag karne ke liye zyada energy chahiye, jis se boiling point barhta aur volatility kam hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Volatility is inversely related to the boiling point of a substance.

blocks.prompt:
12 Differentiate between small and large halogen molecules in their London forces and physical properties (Table 13.2).
(Chhote aur bare halogen molecules mein London forces aur physical properties ka farq likhein (Table 13.2).)
blocks.explanation: Chhote molecules ki forces kamzor aur volatility zyada; bare molecules ki forces mazboot aur volatility kam:

book_ref.quote: Table 13.2 Effect of London forces on physical properties

blocks.prompt:
13 Why is chlorine a gas while iodine is a solid at room temperature?
(Room temperature par chlorine gas aur iodine solid kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Chlorine ke molecules chhote aur id-id forces kamzor hain, is liye woh gas hain. Iodine ke molecules sab se bare aur zyada polarizable hain, group mein sab se mazboot forces ke saath, is liye iodine solid hai.

book_ref.quote: Iodine has the strongest forces among the group, so it is in solid state at room temperature.

blocks.prompt:
14 Using Table 13.1, find the difference between the boiling points of iodine and bromine and explain it.
(Table 13.1 se iodine aur bromine ke boiling points ka farq nikalein aur wajah batayein.)
blocks.explanation: I₂ ka b.p. = 183 °C, Br₂ = 59 °C; farq = 183 - 59 = 124 °C. Iodine ke molecules bare aur zyada polarizable hain, is liye London forces mazboot hain aur ubalne ke liye zyada energy chahiye.

book_ref.quote: The forces depend on factors like molecular size, shape and polarizability

blocks.text: 13.3 The bond strength of halogen molecules

blocks.prompt:
15 Why does the X-X bond energy decrease from chlorine to iodine?
(Chlorine se iodine tak X-X bond energy kyun kam hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Group mein neeche atomic size barhta hai, is liye bond length lambi aur bond kamzor hota hai: Cl₂ 243, Br₂ 193, I₂ 151 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: increase in the atomic size down the group which results in longer bond lengths and weaker bonds

blocks.prompt:
16 Justify: the F-F bond is weaker than the Cl-Cl bond although fluorine is more electronegative.
(Saabit karein: F-F bond Cl-Cl bond se kamzor hai halaanke fluorine zyada electronegative hai.)
blocks.explanation: Fluorine atoms bohat chhote hain, is liye dono jure atoms ke lone pairs qareeb hote hain aur shadeed repulsion (dhakelna) karte hain. Yeh electron-electron repulsion bond ko kamzor karta hai: F₂ 156 kJ mol⁻¹ jabke Cl₂ 243 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: significant electron–electron repulsion between the lone pairs on the fluorine atoms

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: F atom itna chhota hai ke do F atoms ke lone pairs bohat qareeb aa jate hain. Negative electrons aik doosre ko dhakelte hain, is liye bond ki taqat kam ho jati hai. Chlorine bara hai, us ke lone pairs door rehte hain, is liye Cl-Cl bond F-F se mazboot hai.

blocks.prompt:
17 Arrange F₂, Cl₂, Br₂ and I₂ in decreasing order of bond energy with values.
(F₂, Cl₂, Br₂ aur I₂ ko qeematon ke saath ghat-ti bond energy ki tarteeb mein likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Cl₂ (243) > Br₂ (193) > F₂ (156) > I₂ (151) kJ mol⁻¹. Fluorine apne chhote atoms mein lone-pair repulsion ki wajah se tarteeb se bahar hai.

book_ref.quote: Table 13.3 Bond energies of halogen molecules

blocks.prompt:
18 From Table 13.3, calculate how much the bond energy falls from Cl₂ to Br₂ and from Br₂ to I₂.
(Table 13.3 se Cl₂ se Br₂ aur Br₂ se I₂ tak bond energy ki kami nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Cl₂ → Br₂: 243 - 193 = 50 kJ mol⁻¹. Br₂ → I₂: 193 - 151 = 42 kJ mol⁻¹. Group mein neeche bond energy darja ba darja kam hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Moving from top to bottom in group 17, the bond energy of halogens decreases gradually from chlorine to iodine.

blocks.text: 13.4 Relative reactivities of the halogens as oxidising agents

blocks.prompt:
19 Why do halogens act as oxidizing agents? Give one equation.
(Halogens oxidizing agents kyun hain? Aik equation dein.)
blocks.explanation: Halogens metals aur aksar non-metals se electrons lete hain aur negative halide ions bante hain, is liye doosre element ko oxidize karte hain. Misal: 2Na(s) + Cl₂(g) → 2NaCl(s).

book_ref.quote: All the free halogens act as oxidizing agents when they react with metals and most of non-metals.

blocks.prompt:
20 Write the balanced equations for fluorine displacing bromide and iodide ions.
(Fluorine ke bromide aur iodide ions ko displace karne ki balanced equations likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
F₂(g) + 2Br⁻(aq) → 2F⁻(aq) + Br₂
F₂(g) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2F⁻(aq) + I₂
Aik F₂ do halide ions se do electrons leta hai aur do fluoride ions banata hai.

book_ref.quote: The balanced equations are F₂(g) + 2Cl¹⁻(aq) → 2F¹⁻(aq) + Cl₂(g)

blocks.prompt:
21 Which halide ions can chlorine displace? Give a balanced ionic equation for one.
(Chlorine kaun se halide ions ko displace kar sakta hai? Aik ki balanced ionic equation dein.)
blocks.explanation: Chlorine Br⁻ aur I⁻ ko oxidize karke displace kar sakta hai (F⁻ ko nahi). Misal: Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂.

book_ref.quote: Similarly, chlorine can oxidize and displace Br⁻ and I⁻.

blocks.prompt:
22 Give reason: iodine cannot displace any other halide ion from its solution.
(Wajah batayein: iodine kisi doosre halide ion ko us ke solution se displace nahi kar sakta.)
blocks.explanation: Iodine halogens mein sab se kamzor oxidizing agent hai (sab se kam E°, +0.54 V). Halogen sirf apne neeche wale halide ions ko displace karta hai, aur iodine ke neeche koi aam halogen nahi.

book_ref.quote: Iodine cannot oxidize any halide ion.

blocks.prompt:
23 How do the E° (X₂/X⁻) values show the trend in oxidizing power? Quote the values.
(E° (X₂/X⁻) values oxidizing power ka silsila kaise dikhati hain? Qeematein likhein.)
blocks.explanation: E° F₂ se I₂ tak kam positive hoti hai: F₂ +2.87 V, Cl₂ +1.36 V, Br₂ +1.07 V, I₂ +0.54 V. E° jitni kam positive, oxidizing power utni kamzor, is liye F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.

book_ref.quote: The oxidizing power of halogens can be related to standard electrode potential (E°) values.

blocks.prompt:
24 Name the factors on which the oxidizing power of a halogen depends.
(Halogen ki oxidizing power kin factors par munhasar hai?)
blocks.explanation: Dissociation energy, atoms ki electron affinity, ions ki hydration energy aur heat of vaporization (Br₂ aur I₂ ke liye). Kam dissociation energy, zyada electron affinity aur zyada hydration energy se oxidizing power zyada hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: energy of dissociation, electron affinity of atoms, hydration energies of ions, and heats of vaporization

blocks.prompt:
25 Using Table 13.4, by how much does E° fall from F₂ to I₂? What does it show?
(Table 13.4 se F₂ se I₂ tak E° kitni kam hoti hai? Is se kya zahir hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2.87 - 0.54 = 2.33 V. Yeh bari kami dikhati hai ke fluorine sab se taqatwar oxidizing agent aur iodine sab se kamzor hai.

book_ref.quote: Table 13.4 Standard electrode potential E° (X₂/X⁻)

blocks.text: 13.5 Reactions of the halogens with hydrogen

blocks.prompt:
26 Write the general equation for the reaction of halogens with hydrogen and state the order of reactivity.
(Halogens ke hydrogen se reaction ki aam equation aur reactivity ki tarteeb likhein.)
blocks.explanation: H₂ + X₂ → 2HX, jahan X₂ = F₂, Cl₂, Br₂ ya I₂. Hydrogen ke saath reactivity group mein neeche kam hoti hai: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.

book_ref.quote: When halogen elements react with hydrogen, they produce hydrogen halides.

blocks.prompt:
27 Write the conditions and equations for the reactions of fluorine and chlorine with hydrogen.
(Fluorine aur chlorine ke hydrogen se reactions ki shiraait aur equations likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Fluorine kam temperature par andhere mein bhi dhamake se react karta hai: H₂(g) + F₂(g) → 2HF(g). Chlorine UV light (hν) ya spark mein aasani se react karta hai: H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g).

book_ref.quote: In the presence of UV light or a spark, chlorine reacts readily with hydrogen

blocks.prompt:
28 Differentiate between the reactions of bromine and iodine with hydrogen.
(Bromine aur iodine ke hydrogen se reactions mein farq likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono ko heat chahiye, lekin iodine ko catalyst bhi chahiye aur us ka reaction reversible hai:

book_ref.quote: At high temperature and in presence of a catalyst, iodine reacts with hydrogen

rows: HBr paani mein hydrobromic acid deti hai
HI paani mein hydroiodic acid deti hai

blocks.prompt:
29 What are hydrohalic acids? Name the acid formed by each hydrogen halide.
(Hydrohalic acids kya hain? Har hydrogen halide se banne wale acid ka naam likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Hydrogen halides be-rang gases hain jo paani mein hal ho kar hydrohalic acids banati hain: HF → hydrofluoric acid, HCl → hydrochloric acid, HBr → hydrobromic acid, HI → hydroiodic acid.

book_ref.quote: Hydrogen halides are colourless gases that dissolve in water to form hydrohalic acid.

blocks.prompt:
30 Using Table 13.1 and H = 1, how many grams of HI can form at most from 2.538 g of iodine? Why is the actual yield lower?
(Table 13.1 aur H = 1 se, 2.538 g iodine se zyada se zyada kitne gram HI ban sakti hai? Asal miqdaar kam kyun hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI. I₂ ke moles = 2.538/253.8 = 0.01 mol; HI = 0.02 mol × 127.9 g mol⁻¹ = zyada se zyada 2.558 g. Reaction reversible aur bohat aahista hai, is liye iodine poora tabdeel nahi hota.

book_ref.quote: This is a reversible reaction and occurs very slowly.

blocks.text: 13.6 Relative thermal stabilities of hydrogen halides in terms of their bond strength

blocks.prompt:
31 Give the bond dissociation energies of the H-X bonds and the resulting order of thermal stability.
(H-X bonds ki bond dissociation energies aur un se banne wali thermal stability ki tarteeb likhein.)
blocks.explanation: H-F 569, H-Cl 431, H-Br 366, H-I 299 kJ mol⁻¹. Bond jitna mazboot, halide utni thermally stable: HF > HCl > HBr > HI.

book_ref.quote: The bond dissociation energy of H-F (569 kJ/mol) is the highest among the hydrogen halides.

blocks.prompt:
32 How does orbital overlap explain the weaker H-Br bond compared with H-Cl?
(Orbital overlap se H-Cl ke muqable mein H-Br bond ka kamzor hona kaise samjhaya jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Bromine ka atomic radius chlorine se bara hai, is liye hydrogen aur bromine ke orbitals ka overlap kam hota hai. Is liye H-Br bond (366 kJ mol⁻¹) H-Cl (431 kJ mol⁻¹) se kamzor hai.

book_ref.quote: There is a reduced overlapping of orbitals.

blocks.prompt:
33 Differentiate between HF and HI with respect to bond and thermal stability.
(HF aur HI mein bond aur thermal stability ke lehaz se farq likhein.)
blocks.explanation: HF sab se zyada aur HI sab se kam thermally stable hydrogen halide hai:

book_ref.quote: Hydrogen fluoride (HF) is the most thermally stable hydrogen halide.

rows: Bohat bara iodine atom, kam electronegativity
Bond energy 569 kJ mol⁻¹ (sab se zyada)
Bond energy 299 kJ mol⁻¹ (sab se kam)

blocks.prompt:
34 Using Table 13.5, find the energy needed to break all the H-X bonds in 0.5 mol of HCl and in 0.5 mol of HI.
(Table 13.5 se 0.5 mol HCl aur 0.5 mol HI ke tamam H-X bonds todne ke liye energy nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: HCl: 0.5 × 431 = 215.5 kJ. HI: 0.5 × 299 = 149.5 kJ. HI todne ke liye kam energy chahiye, is liye woh garam karne par aasani se toot-ti hai.

book_ref.quote: Table 13.5 Bond dissociation energy of H-X bonds

blocks.text: 13.7 Relative reactivity of halide ions as reducing agents

blocks.prompt:
35 Arrange the halide ions in decreasing reducing power and state the two properties responsible.
(Halide ions ko ghat-ti reducing power ki tarteeb mein likhein aur zimmedar do properties batayein.)
blocks.explanation: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻. Group mein neeche electronegativity kam aur ionic size zyada hota hai, is liye charge density kam hoti hai aur ion aasani se electron deta hai.

book_ref.quote: The order of decreasing power as a reducing agent is I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻.

blocks.prompt:
36 Why is the fluoride ion the weakest reducing agent?
(Fluoride ion sab se kamzor reducing agent kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Fluorine bohat electronegative hai aur apne extra electron ko mazbooti se pakarta hai. F⁻ chhota hai aur us ki charge density zyada hai jo use mustahkam rakhti hai, is liye woh electron mushkil se deta hai.

book_ref.quote: the strong bond between the fluorine atom and its extra electron make it difficult

blocks.prompt:
37 What is meant by charge density, and how does it affect the reducing power of the iodide ion?
(Charge density se kya murad hai, aur yeh iodide ion ki reducing power par kaise asar dalti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Charge density ion ke size ke muqable mein us ka charge hai. Iodide ion bara hai, is liye us ka aik negative charge phaila hua hai (kam charge density); electron dheela pakra hota hai aur aasani se de diya jata hai, is liye I⁻ taqatwar reducing agent hai.

book_ref.quote: This results in a lower charge density and a tendency to donate an electron by the iodide ion

blocks.prompt:
38 Differentiate between bromide and fluoride ions as reducing agents.
(Bromide aur fluoride ions mein reducing agent ke taur par farq likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Bromide zyada taqatwar reducing agent hai:

book_ref.quote: Bromide ion (Br⁻) has a larger ionic radius and lower charge density

rows: Aasani se electron deta hai; zyada taqatwar reducing agent
Mushkil se electron deta hai; sab se kamzor reducing agent

blocks.text: 13.8 Reactions of halides with aqueous silver ion followed by aqueous ammonia

blocks.prompt:
39 What is the silver nitrate test? Write its correct general ionic equation.
(Silver nitrate test kya hai? Is ki sahi aam ionic equation likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Halide ions ki pehchaan ka test: aqueous AgNO₃ dala jata hai aur insoluble silver halide ka rang halide batata hai. Aam equation: X⁻(aq) + Ag⁺(aq) → AgX(s).

book_ref.quote: These reactions are used in qualitative analysis to identify halides ions.

blocks.prompt:
40 Why can the silver nitrate test not detect fluoride ions by a precipitate?
(Silver nitrate test fluoride ions ko precipitate se kyun nahi pehchan sakta?)
blocks.explanation: Silver fluoride paani mein hal ho jata hai, is liye Ag⁺ aur F⁻ milane par na precipitate banta hai na koi reaction nazar aata hai.

book_ref.quote: As silver fluoride is soluble in water, Fluoride (F⁻) does not form precipitate as silver fluoride.

blocks.prompt:
41 Write the ionic equations and the colours of the precipitates formed by Ag⁺(aq) with chloride and iodide ions.
(Ag⁺(aq) ke chloride aur iodide ions ke saath ionic equations aur precipitates ke rang likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s), safed precipitate.
Ag⁺(aq) + I⁻(aq) → AgI(s), zard precipitate.

book_ref.quote: a white precipitate of silver chloride forms, which is soluble in dilute ammonia

blocks.prompt:
42 Using Ag = 108 and Table 13.1 (Na = 23), find the mass of AgBr precipitated from 2.058 g of NaBr with excess AgNO₃.
(Ag = 108, Na = 23 aur Table 13.1 se, 2.058 g NaBr zyada AgNO₃ ke saath kitna AgBr precipitate dega?)
blocks.explanation: NaBr = 23 + 79.9 = 102.9 g mol⁻¹; moles = 2.058/102.9 = 0.02 mol. Ag⁺ + Br⁻ → AgBr, is liye AgBr = 0.02 mol × 187.9 g mol⁻¹ = 3.758 g.

book_ref.quote: This type of reactions is used to identify halide ions and is called silver nitrate test.

blocks.prompt:
43 Why is aqueous ammonia added after silver nitrate in testing halides?
(Halides ke test mein silver nitrate ke baad aqueous ammonia kyun dala jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Safed, cream aur zard precipitates aik jaise lag sakte hain. Ammonia in ki solubility check karta hai: AgCl dilute NH₃ mein, AgBr sirf concentrated NH₃ mein aur AgI kisi mein hal nahi hota; is se halide ki tasdeeq hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Addition of aqueous ammonia tests the solubility of initially formed silver halide precipitates.

blocks.prompt:
44 Write the equation for silver chloride dissolving in ammonia and name the complex ion formed.
(Silver chloride ke ammonia mein hal hone ki equation likhein aur banne wale complex ion ka naam batayein.)
blocks.explanation: AgCl(s) + 2NH₃(aq) → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq). Complex ion [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ diamminesilver(I) ion hai; solution be-rang hota hai.

book_ref.quote: The white precipitate of AgCl dissolves in dilute ammonia forming a colourless solution.

blocks.prompt:
45 Differentiate between silver chloride and silver bromide.
(Silver chloride aur silver bromide mein farq likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono insoluble silver halides hain lekin rang aur ammonia mein solubility mein farq hai:

book_ref.quote: The cream-coloured precipitate of AgBr dissolves in concentrated ammonia

rows: Cl⁻ aur Ag⁺ se banta hai
Br⁻ aur Ag⁺ se banta hai
Sirf concentrated aqueous ammonia mein hal

blocks.prompt:
46 A solution gives a pale yellow precipitate with AgNO₃(aq) which does not dissolve in concentrated ammonia. Identify the halide ion and write the equation.
(Aik solution AgNO₃(aq) se halka zard precipitate deta hai jo concentrated ammonia mein bhi hal nahi hota. Halide ion pehchanein aur equation likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Halide ion iodide, I⁻ hai. Ag⁺(aq) + I⁻(aq) → AgI(s); silver iodide na dilute na concentrated ammonia mein hal hota hai.

book_ref.quote: does not dissolve in both dilute and concentrated ammonia

blocks.text: 13.9 Reactions of halides (X-) with concentrated sulfuric acid

blocks.prompt:
47 Write the equation for concentrated sulfuric acid with sodium fluoride. Why does the reaction stop at HF?
(Concentrated sulfuric acid aur sodium fluoride ki equation likhein. Reaction HF par kyun ruk jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: NaF(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄ + HF(g); HF ke fumes nazar aate hain. HF kamzor reducing agent hai, is liye H₂SO₄ ko reduce nahi kar sakti aur aage react nahi karti.

book_ref.quote: Fumes of hydrogen fluoride gas are produced when concentrated sulfuric acid reacts with NaF.

blocks.prompt:
48 Write the two equations for the reaction of sodium bromide with concentrated sulfuric acid.
(Sodium bromide aur concentrated sulfuric acid ke reaction ki do equations likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
NaBr + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄ + HBr(g)
2HBr(g) + H₂SO₄(l) → Br₂(g) + SO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)
Doosre qadam mein HBr acid ko SO₂ mein reduce karti hai aur khud Br₂ mein oxidize hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Hydrogen bromide acts as a reducing agent by reducing sulfuric acid to sulfur dioxide and is self-oxidized to bromine.

blocks.prompt:
49 Show the change in oxidation states of iodine and sulfur in the reaction of HI with concentrated sulfuric acid.
(HI aur concentrated sulfuric acid ke reaction mein iodine aur sulfur ki oxidation states ki tabdeeli dikhayein.)
blocks.explanation: 8HI(g) + H₂SO₄(l) → 4I₂(s) + H₂S(g) + 4H₂O(l). Iodine: -1 (HI) → 0 (I₂), oxidize hua. Sulfur: +6 (H₂SO₄) → -2 (H₂S), 8 units reduce hua; 8 I atoms aik aik electron dete hain.

book_ref.quote: 8HI(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → 4I₂(s) + H₂S(g) + 4H₂O(l)

blocks.prompt:
50 Differentiate between the reactions of concentrated sulfuric acid with NaCl and with NaI.
(Concentrated sulfuric acid ke NaCl aur NaI ke saath reactions mein farq likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Chloride sirf HCl deta hai; iodide aage redox reaction karta hai:

book_ref.quote: When concentrated sulfuric acid reacts with sodium chloride, fumes of hydrogen chloride gas are produced.

rows: HI ke fumes, iodine ke banafshi fumes, H₂S ki boo
NaI + H₂SO₄ → NaHSO₄ + HI, phir 8HI + H₂SO₄ → 4I₂ + H₂S + 4H₂O
Redox: HI H₂SO₄ ko H₂S mein reduce karti hai

blocks.prompt:
51 Why do the reactions of halides with concentrated sulfuric acid become more complex from fluoride to iodide?
(Fluoride se iodide tak halides ke concentrated sulfuric acid ke saath reactions zyada pecheeda kyun hote hain?)
blocks.explanation: Reducing power F⁻ se I⁻ tak barhti hai. HF aur HCl acid ko reduce nahi kar sakti; HBr use SO₂ (S +6 → +4) tak aur sab se taqatwar HI use H₂S (S +6 → -2) tak reduce karti hai.

book_ref.quote: leads to more complex reactions with concentrated sulfuric acid

blocks.text: 13.10 Reactions of chlorine with cold and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide

blocks.prompt:
52 What decides whether chlorine forms NaClO or NaClO₃ with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
(Aqueous sodium hydroxide ke saath chlorine NaClO banaye ga ya NaClO₃, yeh kis cheez se tay hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Reaction ka temperature: thanda aqueous NaOH NaCl aur NaClO (sodium chlorate(I)) deta hai; garam aqueous NaOH NaCl aur NaClO₃ (sodium chlorate(V)) deta hai.

book_ref.quote: form different products according to the temperature of the reaction

blocks.prompt:
53 Give the new and old names of NaClO and the oxidation state of chlorine in it.
(NaClO ka naya aur purana naam aur is mein chlorine ki oxidation state batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Naya naam: sodium chlorate(I); purana naam: sodium hypochlorite. Chlorine +1 hai (Na +1, O -2: +1 + x - 2 = 0, x = +1).

book_ref.quote: Sodium chlorate (I) is previously called sodium hypochlorite.

blocks.prompt:
54 Using Table 13.1 and Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1, find the mass of NaOH needed to react completely with 3.55 g of chlorine in the cold.
(Table 13.1 aur Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1 se, thande mein 3.55 g chlorine se poori tarah react karne ke liye kitna NaOH chahiye?)
blocks.explanation: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O. Cl₂ ke moles = 3.55/71.0 = 0.05 mol; NaOH = 2 × 0.05 = 0.1 mol; mass = 0.1 × 40 = 4.0 g.

book_ref.quote: The above reaction shows the simultaneous oxidation and reduction of chlorine

blocks.prompt:
55 In the balanced reaction of chlorine with hot NaOH, show that the electrons lost equal the electrons gained.
(Chlorine aur garam NaOH ki balanced reaction mein dikhayein ke diye gaye electrons liye gaye electrons ke barabar hain.)
blocks.explanation: 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O. Paanch Cl atoms 0 → -1, 5 × 1 = 5 electrons lete hain; aik Cl atom 0 → +5, 5 electrons deta hai. 5 liye = 5 diye.

book_ref.quote: five Cl atoms are reduced to -1 and one is oxidised to +5

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Hot NaOH mein 6 chlorine atoms hain. Har reduce hone wala atom sirf aik electron leta hai (0 se -1), lekin oxidize hone wala atom 5 electrons deta hai (0 se +5). Is liye 5 atoms reduce aur 1 oxidize hota hai, aur NaCl ka coefficient 5 aata hai.

blocks.prompt:
56 Differentiate between the reactions of chlorine with cold and with hot aqueous NaOH.
(Chlorine ke thande aur garam aqueous NaOH ke saath reactions mein farq likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono disproportionation reactions hain, lekin products aur oxidation states mukhtalif hain:

book_ref.quote: Chlorine is oxidized from 0 to +5 in NaClO₃.

blocks.text: 13.11 Use of chlorine in water purification

blocks.prompt:
57 Chlorine gas is very poisonous, yet it is added to drinking water. Explain.
(Chlorine gas bohat zehreeli hai, phir bhi peene ke paani mein dali jati hai. Wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation: Thodi miqdaar mein chlorine insaanon ke liye be-zarar lekin beemari phailane wale bacteria ke liye zehreeli hai. Apni mazboot disinfectant (jaraseem-kush) khasiyat ki wajah se yeh treatment plants par istemal hoti hai, jahan active species (HOCl, OCl⁻) bana kar pathogens ko maarti hai.

book_ref.quote: Chlorine gas is very poisonous.

blocks.prompt:
58 Why is swimming-pool water given a slightly higher chlorine concentration than drinking water?
(Swimming pool ke paani mein peene ke paani se thodi zyada chlorine kyun dali jati hai?)
blocks.explanation: Swimming pool ke paani mein bacteria zyada hone ka imkaan hai, is liye use saaf karne ke liye thodi zyada chlorine chahiye.

book_ref.quote: Water in the swimming pools is also chlorinated

blocks.prompt:
59 Write the equations showing how chlorine in water forms the chlorate(I) ion.
(Equations likhein jo dikhayein ke paani mein chlorine se chlorate(I) ion kaise banta hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Cl₂(g) + H₂O(l) → HCl(aq) + HClO(aq)
HOCl kamzor acid hai aur jazwi tor par toot-ta hai: HOCl ⇌ H⁺ + OCl⁻ (chlorate(I) ion).

book_ref.quote: is a weak acid and partially dissociate in water

blocks.prompt:
60 Give reason: HOCl is a more effective disinfectant than OCl⁻.
(Wajah batayein: HOCl OCl⁻ se zyada moassar disinfectant hai.)
blocks.explanation: HOCl par koi charge nahi (neutral), is liye woh micro-organisms ki cell walls mein aasani se dakhil hota hai; charged OCl⁻ ion itni aasani se nahi.

book_ref.quote: The neutral charge of HOCl allows to penetrate the cell walls of micro-organisms easily.

blocks.prompt:
61 Name three cell parts attacked by HOCl and OCl⁻ and state the result.
(HOCl aur OCl⁻ cell ke jin teen hisson par hamla karte hain un ke naam aur nateeja likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Proteins aur lipids oxidize hote hain, zinda rehne aur replication ke liye zaroori enzymes na-kaara hote hain, aur nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) oxidize hote hain. Cell ka kaam bigar jata hai, bacteria replicate nahi kar sakte aur cell mar jata hai.

book_ref.quote: can oxidize and inactivate enzymes that are crucial for survival and replication of bacteria

blocks.prompt:
62 How does pH affect the disinfection of water by chlorine?
(pH chlorine se paani ki disinfection par kaise asar dalta hai?)
blocks.explanation: pH taqreeban 6-7.5 par HOCl ghalib hota hai aur disinfection zyada moassar hoti hai. pH 7.5 se upar OCl⁻ ghalib hota hai; yeh kam moassar hai lekin phir bhi disinfection karta hai.

book_ref.quote: At higher pH (above 7.5), OCl⁻ predominates, its less effective but still provides disinfection.

blocks.prompt:
63 Why must the contact time of water with chlorine be long enough?
(Paani aur chlorine ka contact time kaafi lamba kyun hona chahiye?)
blocks.explanation: Disinfectants HOCl aur OCl⁻ ko bacteria, viruses aur protozoa mein dakhil ho kar unhein maarne ke liye waqt chahiye; kam contact time mein kuch micro-organisms zinda reh jate hain.

book_ref.quote: to allow the disinfectants to penetrate and kill bacteria, viruses and protozoa
